analysis.investment_thesis: KSB is a quality industrial compounder with zero debt and a German-parent pedigree, but at 58x earnings for a 14–16% grower the PEG ratio is ~3.6x — far beyond my discipline of paying less than 1x. Growth visibly decelerated in FY25 (revenue +6.4%, profit +9.3%) just as the stock commands a premium valuation, which is exactly the wrong combination.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet — net debt is essentially zero (borrowings ₹5 Cr, cash ₹167 Cr), a true fortress.
ROCE of 24.5% and consistent operating margin expansion (~14.5%) show a disciplined, capital-efficient business.
Diversified end-markets (water, wastewater, energy, chemicals, oil & gas) with India's infrastructure capex cycle as a structural tailwind.
key_risks: Valuation is the biggest risk — P/E 58x on a ~14% earner gives PEG ~3.6x; I never pay more than 1x the growth rate.
Growth is decelerating sharply: FY25 revenue grew only 6.4% and net profit only 9.3%, the weakest prints in the dataset.
Free cash flow collapsed to near zero in FY25 (OCF ₹93 Cr vs. net profit ₹270 Cr) — profits aren't converting to cash.
red_flags: PEG ratio ~3.6x — more than triple my maximum threshold of 1.0x.
FY25 OCF/Net profit conversion of only 34% is a serious earnings quality warning.
Revenue growth slowed to 6.4% in FY25 — if this is the new run-rate, the stalwart label is generous and the current multiple is indefensible.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KSB Limited is a textbook stalwart — a 65-year-old industrial company with steady compounding, zero debt, and a world-class German parent (KSB SE) owning ~70%. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 14% and net profit CAGR of 16.4% are respectable, and ROCE of 24.5% confirms genuine capital efficiency. The product mix — pumps and valves for water, power, chemicals, and decarbonization — is exactly the kind of boring, essential infrastructure business I like. I'd happily own this at the right price.

The right price, however, is not 58x earnings. My PEG calculation — P/E of 58.3 divided by a growth rate I'm most generously pegging at 16% — lands at 3.6x, which is egregiously expensive. Worse, FY25 is flashing real deterioration: top-line growth fell to 6.4%, earnings growth to 9.3%, and free cash flow went to zero as capex (₹94 Cr) consumed all operating cash generation. At EV/EBITDA of 44x, the market is pricing this as a fast grower when the data says it's slowing. The story has weakened at exactly the moment the stock demands a perfect story. Wait for a 40–50% correction to bring the PEG below 1.5x before getting interested.
